coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the OpenStreetMap outline of the plant. The shallow underground laboratory was 750-890 m from the reactors (inside the plant area or just outside it); no fetched source gives its coordinate.

depth_mwe.quote: The 32 meter-waterequivalent overburden entirely eliminated any hadronic component of cosmic radiation and reduced the cosmic muon flux.

summary.plain: A shallow underground laboratory near the Palo Verde nuclear power station in Arizona, 750 to 890 metres from its three reactors and under 32 metres of water-equivalent rock, where the Palo Verde detector ran from 1998 to 2000.
summary.technical: Shallow underground site 890 m from two of the Palo Verde reactors and 750 m from the third, under 32 m.w.e. overburden. Marked with a campus-grade point for the plant.
